column1: # MODULES (G6 phase 2, docs/capability-review/g6-distribution.md). An
# import is still just `@"…"`; the string's SHAPE routes it, so the
# grammar is untouched and every existing include keeps its behaviour.
# Columns: name<TAB>mode<TAB>src<TAB>expect
# These rows run against real fixture trees under
# `test/spec/files/mod*/`, and under the FIXTURES trust root, exactly as
# file.tsv's do — a module is resolved from the filesystem, so proving
# it needs a filesystem.
# EVALUATION NEVER TOUCHES THE NETWORK: resolution reads `aon_vendor/`
# beside the project's `mod.aon` and a content-addressed user cache, and
# nothing else. A module in neither store is an error that names the
# fetch step; a module whose MEANING disagrees with its pin is an
# integrity error naming both hashes.
mod-vendor
mod-vendor-canon
mod-lock-pin
mod-inline-pin
mod-file-is-a-document
mod-missing
mod-missing-message

# A module resolves from ITS OWN project root FIRST, and then from the
# roots that enclose it -- because a vendored module is a project
# inside a project, and `mod vendor` only ever produces a FLAT tree, so
# a nested import has nowhere else to find its dependency
# (use-cases/BUGS.md §31). The vendored module here imports ITSELF: it
# used to answer `module not fetched`, which was the upward walk
# stopping early rather than a fact about the document, and now the
# import is found and refused as what it is -- a source cannot be its
# own ancestor.
mod-nested-has-its-own-root
# THE ROUTING GUARD. A path routes to the module resolver only when it
# is domain-shaped AND carries a major; anything else falls through the
# chain exactly as it did before this phase existed.
mod-no-major-is-not-a-module
mod-no-dot-is-not-a-module
mod-shaped-is-a-module

column1: # THE MODULE FILE'S OWN EDGES. A module file with no `main` uses the
# default entry (`main.aon`); one naming an entry that is not there is
# the same refusal an absent module is, because the module is not
# there to be read. A module file that does not stand up has no
# metadata to read either — the default entry stands rather than the
# read failing.
mod-default-entry
mod-entry-not-there
mod-file-unreadable-uses-default
# A LOCKFILE IS GENERATED, and only a generated one is read: canonical
# Aontu whose leaves are scalars IS JSON, so a hand-edited lockfile
# that is no longer canonical does not parse — and an entry with no
# `canon` pin has nothing to check. Neither is an error: what is
# missing is the PIN, and a module with no pin is simply unpinned.
mod-lockfile-not-canonical
mod-lock-entry-without-pin
# TWO MISSING MODULES, ONE REFUSAL: the FIRST is the one reported, as
# the first denied include is. A refusal is about the document not
# standing up, and the second miss adds nothing to that.
mod-first-miss-is-the-one
mod-first-miss-message
